Without breaking down your code, I believe this is where we diverge:

if prize == choices[0]: #makes sure the remaining door to be eliminated is not the prize door

This is the exploit of the Monty Hall Problem.

If you didn't pick the winning door (66% chance) then the only door Monty can eliminate after that is the other losing door, in which case switching gives you a 100% chance of winning.

If you did pick the winning door (33% chance), then Monty can eliminate either of the remaining doors, in which case switching gives you a 0% chance of winning.

But at no point can he eliminate the winning door.

Therefore switching gives roughly a 66% chance of winning.
